sections.chapter_title: Temperature, Kinetic Theory, and the Gas Laws
sections.title: Temperature
learning_objectives: Define temperature.
Convert temperatures between the Celsius, Fahrenheit, and Kelvin scales.
Define thermal equilibrium.
State the zeroth law of thermodynamics.

sections.chapter_title: Temperature, Kinetic Theory, and the Gas Laws
sections.title: Thermal Expansion of Solids and Liquids
learning_objectives: Define and describe thermal expansion.
Calculate the linear expansion of an object given its initial length, change in temperature, and coefficient of linear expansion.
Calculate the volume expansion of an object given its initial volume, change in temperature, and coefficient of volume expansion.
Calculate thermal stress on an object given its original volume, temperature change, volume change, and bulk modulus.

sections.chapter_title: Temperature, Kinetic Theory, and the Gas Laws
sections.title: The Ideal Gas Law
learning_objectives: State the ideal gas law in terms of molecules and in terms of moles.
Use the ideal gas law to calculate pressure change, temperature change, volume change, or the number of molecules or moles in a given volume.
Use Avogadro’s number to convert between number of molecules and number of moles.

sections.chapter_title: Temperature, Kinetic Theory, and the Gas Laws
sections.title: Kinetic Theory: Atomic and Molecular Explanation of Pressure and Temperature
learning_objectives: Express the ideal gas law in terms of molecular mass and velocity.
Define thermal energy.
Calculate the kinetic energy of a gas molecule, given its temperature.
Describe the relationship between the temperature of a gas and the kinetic energy of atoms and molecules.
Describe the distribution of speeds of molecules in a gas.

sections.chapter_title: Temperature, Kinetic Theory, and the Gas Laws
sections.title: Phase Changes
learning_objectives: Interpret a phase diagram.
State Dalton’s law.
Identify and describe the triple point of a gas from its phase diagram.
Describe the state of equilibrium between a liquid and a gas, a liquid and a solid, and a gas and a solid.

sections.chapter_title: Temperature, Kinetic Theory, and the Gas Laws
sections.title: Humidity, Evaporation, and Boiling
learning_objectives: Explain the relationship between vapor pressure of water and the capacity of air to hold water vapor.
Explain the relationship between relative humidity and partial pressure of water vapor in the air.
Calculate vapor density using vapor pressure.
Calculate humidity and dew point.

misconception.text: Temperature is the same thing as heat.

correction.text: Temperature measures how hot a body is, the average kinetic energy of its particles. Heat is the energy that moves because of a temperature difference.

signal.text: Our own teaching of the section, waiting for a paper question that shows the same mistake.

misconception.text: The pressure of a gas depends only on its temperature.

correction.text: It depends on the temperature and on the volume, which is what the gas laws state.
